components.name: k6 generator
components.summary: Produces controlled traffic outside the AWS cluster.
components.description: The cp-bcc daemon runs bounded k6 profiles against the public Laravel endpoint. Its heartbeat reports the profile and virtual users actually running, separately from a pending dashboard request.
components.why: Keeping the load source outside Kubernetes avoids consuming the resources being evaluated.
components.failure: An old heartbeat means execution is unknown. An accepted override alone does not prove a profile switch.

components.name: Caddy ingress
components.summary: Terminates HTTPS and routes public domains to NodePorts.
components.description: Caddy runs on the control-plane host, in front of the Kubernetes application services. Cloudflare-proxied domains reach Caddy, which forwards requests to the configured service NodePort.
components.why: One ingress layer gives the dashboard, model API, registry, storage and application consistent public URLs.
interfaces: Host service; not a Kubernetes pod
components.failure: This explorer does not probe the Caddy process or verify TLS independently. Its role is configured; Kubernetes node readiness is a different signal.

components.name: Laravel API
components.summary: The PHP-FPM workload whose replicas are scaled.
components.description: Laravel serves the application through an Nginx/PHP-FPM pod. The predictive scaler changes this Deployment's replica count; observed pod placement here comes from Kubernetes, not from a simulated architecture diagram.
components.why: This is the application capacity the forecast and scaling policy are intended to protect.
components.failure: Running phase does not mean every container is Ready. Compare ready containers, restarts and the current node before investigating application latency.

components.name: Prometheus
components.summary: Collects telemetry used by inference and training.
components.description: Prometheus collects application and infrastructure metrics. The controller queries current request rate, CPU, latency and memory; continuous training ingests a time window through query_range.
components.why: One observed telemetry source connects online scaling decisions with the training dataset.
components.failure: Stale or missing series can degrade the control loop even when the Prometheus pod is Ready. Pod health is not a query-freshness guarantee.

components.name: Predictive scaler
components.summary: Turns observed telemetry and forecasts into replica changes.
components.description: The scaler runs beside inference in the same pod. It reads Prometheus, submits /scale-decision, applies bounded replicas through the Kubernetes API, and records actual applied scaling events. Scale-down uses a cooldown.
components.why: The model recommends capacity; this controller owns the action and policy boundary.
components.failure: A recent decision means the loop is active; it does not prove every recommendation was applied. Applied action records and pod readiness are separate evidence.

components.name: Inference API
components.summary: Serves the loaded champion and forecasts workload +60 seconds.
components.description: FastAPI loads an exact MLflow registry version into memory, predicts request rate at a 60-second horizon, and exposes operational reads. Strict hot reload keeps the existing serving model if loading fails.
components.why: Serving version and registry alias must agree before a training operation can claim delivery.
components.failure: Model ready describes the loaded artifact. Dependency reachability, feature freshness and end-to-end SLO require separate checks.

components.name: Kubernetes API
components.summary: Schedules pods and reconciles Deployments and training Jobs.
components.description: K3s runs the Kubernetes control plane. The scaler patches application replicas and the retraining worker creates an owned Job from the deployed CronJob template. Nodes report readiness and allocatable capacity to this API.
components.why: Desired replicas become real application capacity only after scheduling and container readiness.
components.failure: Ready nodes may still have insufficient allocatable resources or unschedulable workloads. This view shows declared capacity, not measured utilization.

components.name: MLOps dashboard
components.summary: Combines read-only telemetry with explicit operational controls.
components.description: The console reads inference, registry summaries, cluster inventory and daemon heartbeat. Workload injection and retraining are explicit user actions. Exploring this map never starts traffic, retrains a model or patches Kubernetes.
components.why: Operators can inspect evidence and understand the effect of a control before using it.
interfaces: Local component → hover, selection and filters
components.failure: A reachable UI does not prove all data sources are healthy. Failed sources stay unknown rather than being filled with demo observations.

components.name: Continuous training
components.summary: Ingests live data, trains candidates and verifies model delivery.
components.description: A CronJob or explicit lifecycle trigger creates a training Job. It ingests Prometheus data, preprocesses and syncs datasets, trains four candidates, evaluates the best against the serving champion on a shared chronological holdout, and verifies registration before promotion and reload.
components.why: A completed job and verified loaded version provide stronger delivery evidence than a trigger acknowledgement.
components.failure: An accepted trigger is not completion. Inspect the Job terminal result, evaluation gate and exact loaded version. Completed Jobs may disappear after their retention period.

components.name: MLflow registry
components.summary: Tracks experiments, model versions and champion/challenger aliases.
components.description: MLflow stores experiment and registry metadata in SQLite on the mlops-mlflow-state PVC. New model artifacts live in MinIO. Registration uses the actual MLflow 3 artifact URI and tests the new version before changing the serving alias.
components.why: The registry identifies which immutable artifact should serve; it is separate from the artifact store and the currently loaded model.
components.failure: PVC persistence survives pod replacement but is not a backup for losing its node. A registry version can exist without a retrievable artifact; delivery must be verified.

components.name: MinIO object storage
components.summary: Stores datasets, DVC content hashes and model artifacts.
components.description: The mlops-dvc bucket contains immutable named telemetry datasets, DVC-compatible CAS objects and new MLflow artifacts. Dataset metadata records actual row count, content hash and raw source. A matching CAS object is checked before reporting DVC synchronization.
components.why: Shared storage makes the same training data and model artifact accessible across transient pods.
components.failure: Pod readiness is not a bucket permission or artifact-integrity test. Do not equate a named-object upload with verified CAS synchronization.

components.name: Grafana
components.summary: Explores longer telemetry windows and operational trends.
components.description: Grafana visualizes Prometheus series for application workload, latency, replicas and infrastructure. Use it for time-window investigation beyond the dashboard's small recent-decision buffer.
components.why: A single latest observation cannot establish window-wide compliance or explain an earlier incident.
components.failure: A Ready Grafana pod does not prove every datasource or dashboard query works. Check query time ranges and missing series.

flows.name: Serving & scaling
flows.description: Follow incoming requests, observed telemetry and the decision that changes application replicas.

flows.name: Training & registry
flows.description: Follow live ingestion, shared artifacts, a validation gate and the champion loaded into serving.

flows.name: Observability
flows.description: Separate workload and serving observations from the views that help an operator investigate them.
